# tinyget

A vibe-coded siimple and naive utility made to save me from messing with some of the Winget CLI commands, with the UI inspired by Endfield.

For full support of Winget and other Windows package managers, check UniGetUI.

# The following are generated by AI

A small desktop front end for [`winget`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
on Windows, written in Rust with [Slint](https://slint.dev).

See what can be upgraded, tick the packages you want, and run the upgrade in a
real terminal window. Hold packages back with winget's own pins.

## What it does

**Upgrades** — lists everything `winget upgrade` reports, with the installed and
available versions side by side. Filter by name or identifier, tick what you
want, and press **Upgrade**.

The upgrade runs as a **single** `winget upgrade` command with every selected
identifier passed positionally, in a **new terminal window** hosted by whatever
you have set as your default terminal application:

```
winget upgrade Comfy.ComfyUI-Desktop Rustlang.Rustup --exact --include-unknown
```

It is deliberately *not* silent, and deliberately does not pass
`--accept-package-agreements`. Installer UI, licence prompts and elevation all
appear in front of you rather than being answered on your behalf. The window
stays open when the run finishes so failures are readable. The exact command is
shown in the app before you press the button.

**While it runs**, the list goes read-only — refresh, the upgrade button, the
tick boxes and every pin button are disabled, and the header rule shows an
activity strip. That is not only cosmetic: winget serialises, so a pin issued
during an install would block on winget's own lock and look like a hang.

The app does not merely fire and forget. The batch file writes winget's exit code
to a sentinel file *before* it pauses, so "winget finished" and "you dismissed the
window" stay separate events — the app unlocks and rescans the moment winget is
done, while the terminal stays open for you to read. If the window is closed
early instead, the child process ending is the fallback signal. Per-package
progress is not available: one `winget upgrade` invocation reports as a whole.

**Pins** — pin a package to hold it back, in either of winget's two modes:

| Mode | Effect | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pinning | Held back from bulk upgrades; a direct upgrade still works | `winget pin add --id <id> --exact` |
| Blocking | Refuses every upgrade until the pin is removed | `winget pin add --id <id> --exact --blocking` |

A pinned package leaves the upgrade list immediately, because `winget upgrade`
already excludes both pin types unless `--include-pinned` is passed — there is no
client-side filter that could drift out of sync with winget's own view. Removing
a pin puts the package back.

Winget's third pin type, **Gating** (`--version 1.2.*`), is displayed if a pin
like that already exists, but tinyget does not offer it as a choice.

## Building

Needs a Rust toolchain and Windows 10 1709 or newer (for winget itself, and for
the Bahnschrift font).

```
cargo build --release      # target/release/tinyget.exe
cargo run                  # debug build, keeps a console for logging
cargo test                 # parser tests, no winget calls
```

## Notes on parsing winget

`winget upgrade` and `winget pin list` have no machine-readable output, so both
are read back from the aligned text table. Three things matter, and all three are
covered by tests in `src/winget.rs`:

- Output is **UTF-8** even when redirected, which is what makes this workable.
- The table is aligned by **display width**, not character count — a CJK glyph
  occupies two cells — so rows are cut with `unicode-width`.
- Column headers are **localized**. The header is found relative to the `-----`
  rule rather than by matching names. Where a localized header label contains a
  space (English `Pin type`), header-based column detection would see an extra
  column, so parsing falls back to splitting from the right: only the leftmost
  field, the package name, can contain spaces.

Rows are validated by their identifier column, which keeps trailing summary lines
("7 upgrades available.") out of the results — winget prints them directly under
the table with no blank line between.

Pin-type values (`Pinning` / `Blocking` / `Gating`) are English in every locale,
so they are safe to match on.
